title: Stranded juvenile sea lion: seizures, hunched posture and dark urine
presentation: Juvenile male California sea lion stranded on a beach, brought into a rescue centre. Hunched, reluctant to move, drinking sea water at the pool edge, and he seizured briefly during admission.

stages.title: Assess the casualty
stages.briefing: Thin, BCS 2/5, dehydrated with tacky gums. Hunched with a tucked abdomen, painful on lumbar palpation, stiff gait. One generalised seizure of 40 seconds on admission. Urine passed is dark and scant. Temperature 38.9°C. Mild conjunctivitis. Stranded during a season with several similar strandings reported along the coast.
stages.prompt: Which findings shape the differential list?

options.label: Hunched posture with lumbar pain and scant dark urine
options.detail: Renal pain and impaired urine production

options.label: Seizure activity in a dehydrated, azotaemic-looking animal
options.detail: Uraemic or toxic encephalopathy

options.label: A cluster of similar strandings along the coast
options.detail: An outbreak or an environmental toxin

options.label: Mild conjunctivitis
options.detail: Common in stranded animals and non-specific

options.label: Temperature 38.9°C
options.detail: Within the expected range for the species

stages.explanation: Two diagnoses dominate stranded Californian sea lions and this history contains both: leptospirosis, which gives renal pain and azotaemia, and domoic acid toxicosis, which gives seizures. The cluster along the coast fits either — an outbreak of one, or an algal bloom producing the other — so the work-up has to separate them rather than choose.

stages.title: Choose the tests
stages.briefing: The animal is sedated for handling and you can sample fully.

options.label: Urea, creatinine and electrolytes
options.detail: Grades the azotaemia and guides fluids

options.label: Leptospira microscopic agglutination test with urine PCR
options.detail: Serology plus shedding status

options.label: Urinalysis with sediment examination
options.detail: Casts, protein, concentrating ability

options.label: Haematology
options.detail: Inflammatory response and anaemia

options.label: Domoic acid assay on urine or serum where available, with hippocampal imaging if possible
options.detail: The other cause of seizures in this species

options.label: Canine distemper virus serology as the primary test
options.detail: Morbillivirus matters in pinnipeds, but it does not explain renal pain with azotaemia first

options.label: Faecal parasitology as a priority
options.detail: Common findings, no bearing on seizures and renal failure

stages.explanation: The plan is built to distinguish two diseases with one overlap: leptospirosis is confirmed by serology and urine PCR, domoic acid by assay and by the hippocampal changes it leaves. Both are zoonotic or public-health relevant in their own way, and Leptospira shedding changes how the centre handles this animal from admission onwards.

stages.title: Interpret the results
stages.briefing: Urea 58 mmol/L (markedly raised), creatinine 780 µmol/L (markedly raised), potassium 5.9 mmol/L, sodium 152 mmol/L. Urinalysis: USG 1.012, protein 3+, granular casts, no glucose. Haematology: neutrophilia with a left shift, mild anaemia. Leptospira MAT titre 1:6,400 to serovar Pomona; urine PCR positive. Domoic acid not detected in urine. Hippocampal imaging not available. Liver enzymes mildly raised, bilirubin normal.
stages.prompt: Which conclusions do these results support?

options.label: Acute kidney injury with severe azotaemia
options.detail: Urea 58 mmol/L, creatinine 780 µmol/L, casts and isosthenuria

options.label: Leptospirosis, serovar Pomona, with active shedding
options.detail: A MAT titre of 1:6,400 with a positive urine PCR

options.label: The seizure is most likely uraemic rather than toxic
options.detail: Domoic acid not detected, with profound azotaemia present

options.label: This animal is a zoonotic risk to staff
options.detail: Shedding leptospires in urine

options.label: Domoic acid toxicosis is confirmed
options.detail: Not detected on assay

options.label: Chronic kidney disease is the diagnosis
options.detail: The picture is acute, with an inflammatory response and a high titre

stages.explanation: Testing for both diseases is what allows a clean answer: the negative domoic acid assay lets you attribute the seizure to uraemia, which changes the treatment from anticonvulsant supportive care to aggressive fluid therapy and antibiotics. The positive urine PCR is the finding that protects the people working with him.

stages.title: Commit to a diagnosis
stages.briefing: Urea 58 mmol/L, creatinine 780 µmol/L, isosthenuria with granular casts and proteinuria, Leptospira Pomona MAT 1:6,400 with positive urine PCR, domoic acid not detected.

options.label: Leptospirosis (serovar Pomona) with acute kidney injury and uraemic seizure
options.detail: Confirmed infection with its renal and neurological consequences

options.label: Domoic acid toxicosis
options.detail: Assay negative

options.label: Chronic kidney disease from an unrelated cause
options.detail: The presentation and serology are acute

options.label: Morbillivirus infection
options.detail: Untested and unsupported by these findings

options.label: Starvation-related metabolic collapse
options.detail: Does not produce a MAT titre of 1:6,400 or granular casts

stages.explanation: The diagnosis drives three separate actions: intravenous fluids with penicillin or doxycycline for the animal, barrier precautions and staff briefing for a shedding zoonosis, and a report into the stranding network — because a Pomona outbreak along a coastline is population-level information that individual centres are uniquely placed to detect.
